study.title: Integrating Convolutional, Transformer, and Graph Neural Networks for Precision Agriculture and Food Security
study.short_title: AgroVisionNet hybrid CNN-ViT-GNN: IoU 87.8, F1 91.6, 115M params on Colab T4

segmentation.domain: general precision-agriculture framework (AgroVisionNet: triple-hybrid CNN + ViT + GNN) benchmarked across five datasets; primary domain here is UAV crop-vs-weed segmentation; also leaf-level disease detection (PlantVillage), field-scale anomaly segmentation (Agriculture-Vision) and land-cover classification (BigEarthNet, EuroSAT)
models_tested: AgroVisionNet (proposed: ResNet-50 CNN + ViT-Base/16 + GraphSAGE GNN)
segmentation.best_model: AgroVisionNet on the UAV Crop and Weed dataset: Accuracy 91.5%, Precision 92.0, Recall 91.2, F1 91.6, IoU 87.8, AUC 95.2, MAE 1.4, C-Index 93.9 (Table 7); also strongest on Agriculture-Vision (Acc 94.5%, IoU 90.3%) and EuroSAT (Acc 96.4%, IoU 92.9%). Outperforms all 9 baselines statistically (Wilcoxon, T=0<2). 115M params total.

dataset.name: UAV Crop and Weed dataset (CropAndWeed, Steininger et al. 2023): 8034 high-resolution UAV-annotated images of maize, sugar beet, sunflower and soy crops with broadleaf/grassy weeds; original labels split into 8 crop and 16 weed classes, with bounding boxes, segmentation masks and stem annotations
dataset.note: Primary RQ1 dataset. Segmentation outputs reformulated as multi-label classification with sigmoid activation (incl. Agriculture-Vision and UAV Crop-Weed). Secondary UAV-relevant dataset: Agriculture-Vision (94,986 RGB+NIR aerial images, 9 anomaly classes, Acc 94.5%, IoU 90.3%). Non-UAV: PlantVillage (54,306 leaf images, 38 crop-disease pairs), BigEarthNet (549,488 Sentinel-1/2 patches, 19 classes), EuroSAT (27,000 Sentinel-2, 10 classes). All inputs resized to 224x224, Adam lr 1e-3 cosine, batch 32, 100 epochs, 70/15/15 split, AMP.

classes: 8 crop classes (e.g., maize, sugar beet, sunflower, soy)
segmentation.backbone: ResNet-50 (ImageNet-1k, 25M params, 3.8 GFLOPs) CNN local encoder + ViT-Base/16 (86M, 17.6 GFLOPs) global encoder + GraphSAGE (4M, 0.6 GFLOPs) relational encoder over a 196-node patch graph (k-NN k=8 + cosine-sim >=0.7 feature edges); learnable alpha fusion + MLP head

mIoU.quote: Table 7 highlight that AgroVisionNet outperforms other models on the UAV Crop and Weed dataset, achieving the highest accuracy (91.5%), IoU (87.8%), AUC (95.2%), and C-Index (93.9%)
mIoU.ambiguity: Mean IoU for the UAV Crop and Weed benchmark (IoU heatmaps across 10 fine-grained crop and weed categories); note segmentation was reformulated as multi-label sigmoid classification, so IoU derives from that setting (U-Net style head used for Agriculture-Vision/UAV datasets per Table 2).

mPA.ambiguity: Accuracy is overall sample/image accuracy, not per-class mean.

F1.quote: AgroVisionNet outperforms other models on the UAV Crop and Weed dataset, achieving the highest accuracy (91.5%), IoU (87.8%) ... F1-Score 91.6
F1.ambiguity: Macro-averaged F1 over the classification/segmentation setup on UAV Crop and Weed.

Dice.ambiguity: Dice loss/score used in training (Dice + BCE), but Dice metric not reported in tables.

PA.quote: AgroVisionNet outperforms other models on the UAV Crop and Weed dataset, achieving the highest accuracy (91.5%)
PA.ambiguity: Overall accuracy on the UAV Crop and Weed benchmark (multi-label reformulation).

weed_F1.ambiguity: Aggregate F1 reported only; no separate weed-class vs crop-class F1 breakdown.

crop_F1.ambiguity: Aggregate F1 reported only; no per-crop-class F1 breakdown.

edge.device: Google Colab T4 GPU (training and inference); edge deployment not implemented - paper argues feasibility on NVIDIA Jetson / Coral TPU via quantization, pruning and knowledge distillation (up to 40% size reduction) without significant accuracy loss
edge.framework: PyTorch 2.x; timm ViT-B/16; PyG (GraphSAGE/GAT); CUDA 12; Adam lr 1e-3, cosine decay, batch 32, 100 epochs

fps.ambiguity: FPS not reported; per-image latency on Colab T4 indicates near real-time feasibility for UAV deployment.

latency_ms.quote: Inference latency averaged 18 ms per 224 x 224 image (batch size = 32), confirming real-time feasibility for UAV and field-robot deployment
latency_ms.ambiguity: Measured on Google Colab T4 GPU at 224x224 (Table 11: 18.5 ms, 440 MB size), NOT on an embedded/edge device; edge.reported=false. If deployed edge-side this would be ~54 FPS equivalent, but no edge measurement exists.

params_M.quote: the total model footprint reaches approximately 115 M parameters and 22 GFLOPs per inference
params_M.ambiguity: Composed of ResNet-50 (25M) + ViT-Base/16 (86M) + GraphSAGE (4M); approx. 1.7x a stand-alone ViT (86M).

gflops.quote: the total model footprint reaches approximately 115 M parameters and 22 GFLOPs per inference
gflops.ambiguity: ResNet-50 3.8 + ViT-B/16 17.6 + GraphSAGE 0.6 = ~22 GFLOPs per 224x224 image; structural estimate.

issues: Multi-dataset benchmark; UAV Crop and Weed selected as the primary RQ1 dataset, but Agriculture-Vision (Acc 94.5%, IoU 90.3%) is equally UAV-relevant; also PlantVillage (IoU 95.6), BigEarthNet (IoU 88.5), EuroSAT (IoU 92.9).

Segmentation datasets were reformulated as multi-label sigmoid classification for training; reported IoU derives from this setting (segmentation head in Table 2 used for Agriculture-Vision/UAV datasets).
Edge.reported=false: latency 18.5 ms measured on Colab T4 GPU, not on an edge/UAV device; Jetson/Coral feasibility is only a claim (compression not applied in experiments).
Wilcoxon significance at alpha=0.20 (non-standard) with critical value 2; all comparisons T=0 favor AgroVisionNet.
